seo_description: Free, open-source macOS menu bar app. Press one hotkey repeatedly to cycle a window through half, two-thirds and one-third widths, edge by edge.
hero_sub: Press Control-Option-Left again and again to cycle a window through half, two-thirds and one-third of the screen. Right, Top and Bottom work the same way.
features_sub: One shortcut per direction walks through several sizes, so you only need to remember a handful of keys.

features.title: Cycling edge hotkeys
features.desc: Left, Right, Top and Bottom each step through 1/2, 2/3 and 1/3 when you repeat the shortcut within the timeout, then return to half.

features.title: Editable cycles
features.desc: Give each direction its own ordered list of up to 6 steps, chosen from 1/4, 1/3, 1/2, 2/3 and 3/4. Set the gap to 0-40 pt and the reset timeout to 0.5-5 seconds.

features.title: Multi-display aware
features.desc: Fractions come from the visible frame of the display the window mostly sits on, excluding the menu bar and Dock. Next Display moves a window across screens, keeping its relative position and size.

features.title: Maximize, Restore and Center
features.desc: Maximize toggles back to the window's previous frame. Center cycles 60%, 80% and the original size.

features.title: Careful with your windows
features.desc: Repeats only advance if the window is still where the app put it. Full-screen windows are skipped, non-resizable windows are only moved, and steps a window's minimum size blocks are skipped.

features.title: Menu bar app with a layout HUD
features.desc: A brief overlay names the layout, such as Left 2/3, and can be turned off. The menu lists every action and its hotkey, and the shortcut recorder warns about likely system conflicts.

permissions_step: Grant Accessibility access when prompted, or later in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility, so the app can move and resize windows.

faq.q: Is SizeCycleKeys really free and open source?
faq.a: Yes. It is released under the MIT license, has no paid tier, and contains no analytics or third-party dependencies. If it saves you time, you can optionally support development through the Support button.

Only Accessibility, which lets it read the focused window's position and size, move and resize it, and check whether a text field has focus. It does not request Screen Recording, Camera, Microphone, Location or network access.
Your shortcuts, cycles and settings are stored locally in macOS UserDefaults on your Mac. Nothing is sent anywhere, because the app has no network access.
Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account, which this free project does not have. Right-click the app and choose Open once to run it, or build it yourself from source with Xcode.
